note: A VHDL case statement reaching the emitter through vhdl2hif, which none of the Verilog case fixtures does. The point of interest is `when others`: VHDL requires the choices to be exhaustive so it is always present, and it has to come out as `default` rather than as the label 2'b11 or as nothing at all. The four alternatives produce four different values under the stimulus, so a selector routed to the wrong branch is a wrong value rather than a coincidence. The stimulus ends by driving the selector to x, which is what separates `default` from an explicit 2'b11 label - VHDL's others covers the metavalues too, and without that row the two spellings are indistinguishable.
